description: Who the data on a phone belongs to (Android and iOS). Given the profile registry, one event and the user's answer to any question it raises, the resulting registry, the question asked (`prompt`), the profile whose every entity is queued as a put (`queue_all`), an anonymous profile merged into an existing one (`merge`), the profile that syncs now (`sync`: send its queue, then pull), and the profiles erased. Events: `edit` (a saved change in the active profile), `sign_in`, `sign_out`, `remove_profile` (Settings, Remove from this device) and `account_deleted` (the phone learned the profile's account no longer exists). Rules: before any sign-in there is one anonymous profile whose edits are saved but never queued; the first sign-in asks `anonymous_data` only if that profile has data (`add_to_account` adopts it and queues everything, `erase` replaces it with a fresh profile) and otherwise adopts it silently; signing in with an anonymous profile that has data as an account that already has a profile asks `anonymous_data` too (`add_to_account` merges the anonymous data into that profile, reported in `merge` and, where a case gives the data, `merged_data`: same-name tags fold together locally, a personal record both profiles have gets the union of their tags (the account profile's first, then the anonymous-only ones, deduplicated after folding, capped at 20 with the account's kept), and every merged entity is queued as a put; `erase` discards the anonymous profile), and either way the account's profile becomes active; signing out keeps the active profile, whose later edits are queued but not sent; signing in as an account that has a profile reactivates it without a question; signing in as a new account creates its profile (`new_profile_id`) and leaves the others untouched; removing a profile with unsent changes asks `unsent_changes` first (`remove` or `cancel`); `account_deleted` asks to `remove` or `keep`, and `keep` marks the profile `account_deleted` and drops its unsent commands (for the active profile it also signs out; the profile stays active and usable offline, its edits are saved but never queued, it never syncs, and it can be removed later); removing the active profile signs out and activates the anonymous profile if there is one, or else starts a fresh one. There is at most one anonymous profile at a time. A profile only syncs when the signed-in account equals its account, and every sync request carries that account in X-Awrad-Account. The scenario_NN cases are one story: each starts where the previous one ended.

profiles.description: Every profile on the phone, in creation order. Each is its own local database.

profile_id.description: Local ID, a UUIDv7 made on the phone.

account_id.description: null only for the anonymous profile.

email.description: For display; null for the anonymous profile.

has_data.description: Holds at least one custom dhikr, tag, personal record or goal (the practice policy and the goal order don't count).

has_unsent.description: Its queue holds commands not yet acknowledged.

account_deleted.description: The profile's account no longer exists and the user kept the profile: it stays usable offline, never syncs, and can be removed from Settings.

choice.description: The user's answer when the event asks; null otherwise.

new_profile_id.description: The local ID a profile created by this event gets.

merge_data.description: Only for a case that merges (expect.merge): the tags and personal records of the anonymous profile and of the account's profile. null otherwise.

erased.description: Profiles whose local database is deleted, in registry order.

merge.description: Add to my account when the account already has a profile on this phone: the anonymous profile (from) is merged into it (into). Tags with the same normalized_name fold together locally, onto the account's tag, and every merged entity is queued as a put in the into profile. A personal record both profiles have gets the union of their tag_ids: the account profile's tags first in their order, then the anonymous-only ones, deduplicated after folding and capped at 20 (the account profile's tags always kept). The from profile's database is then deleted, so it is also listed in erased. null otherwise.

merged_data.description: The account profile's tags and personal records after the merge, and the entities queued as puts (in the order queued: tags, then personal records, each in their listed order). null when given.merge_data is null.

cases.description: Scenario step 1. Before any sign-in there is one anonymous profile. An edit is saved there; nothing is queued, because the data belongs to no account yet.

Scenario step 2. The first sign-in (A) finds anonymous data and asks once. Add to my account: the anonymous profile becomes A's, every entity in it is queued as a put, and the phone sends and then pulls A's data.
Scenario step 3. The queue has been sent (after 14). Signing out keeps A's profile active; nothing is erased or sent.
Scenario step 4. Signed out, edits go on being saved and queued for A; they just aren't sent.
Scenario step 5. Signing in as A again asks nothing: A's profile stays active and its queue is sent, then pulled.

Scenario step 6. A signed out with edits still unsent (say the phone was offline). Signing in as B switches to a new profile for B, downloaded fresh; A's profile and its unsent commands stay untouched.
Scenario step 7. B has synced and signed out. Signing in as A makes A's profile active again, with no question, and only now are A's kept commands sent, with A's token.
At the first sign-in the user chooses Erase: the anonymous profile is deleted and A's profile is downloaded fresh into a new one.
An empty anonymous profile needs no question: it simply becomes A's profile and A's data is downloaded into it.

A's profile is on the phone, and the active anonymous profile has data. Signing in as A asks once; Add to my account merges the anonymous data into A's profile (same-name tags fold together locally, every merged entity is queued as a put), erases the anonymous profile and makes A's profile active.

Merging into an existing profile when both profiles tagged the same dhikr: the anonymous "MORNING" tag folds onto the account's "Morning"; the shared record keeps the account's tags in order, then adds the anonymous-only ones, without repeats (at most 20, the account's always kept). The new tag and both changed records are queued as puts; the folded tag isn't.
The same sign-in answered with Erase discards the anonymous data and makes A's profile active as it was.
An empty anonymous profile asks nothing when signing in as an account that has a profile: that profile becomes active and the anonymous one stays, untouched.
Signed in as the active profile's account, an edit is queued and sent (after the debounce).
The profile's display email follows the account's current email at sign-in.
Remove from this device on a profile with unsent changes warns first; confirming erases it, unsent commands included.
Cancelling the warning keeps everything.
A profile with nothing unsent is removed without the warning.
Removing the active profile signs its account out and leaves a fresh, empty anonymous profile active, as on a new install.
Removing the active profile when an anonymous profile is already on the phone signs out and activates that one; no second anonymous profile is made.
When the phone learns that a profile's account no longer exists, it offers to remove that profile; its unsent changes can never be sent, so there's no separate warning.
The user may keep the deleted account's profile on the phone: it's marked account_deleted, its unsent commands are dropped because they can never be sent, and it never syncs again.
If the deleted account is the active, signed-in one, it's signed out; removing its profile leaves a fresh anonymous profile.
Keep for the active profile of a deleted account signs out and drops its unsent commands; the profile stays active and usable offline, marked account_deleted, and never syncs again.
An edit in a kept profile of a deleted account is saved locally only: nothing is queued or sent.
A kept profile of a deleted account can be removed later from Settings. It's the active profile and there's no anonymous one, so a fresh anonymous profile becomes active.
A profile whose only data is goals still asks at the first sign-in: goals are data. The goal order, like the practice policy, isn't.
